Changed this cycle: I tested two Rust no-tail request-cache variants in `src/db.rs`, but neither produced a durable win, so I restored the proven cycle-5 hot path. The kept changes are harness/docs only: [.meta_codex/tools/analyze_request_cache_keys](</__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/.meta_codex/tools/analyze_request_cache_keys:1>) now reports `direct_safe`, and I recorded the outcome in [.meta_codex/research_notes.md](</__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/.meta_codex/research_notes.md:1>) and [.meta_codex/campaign_journal.md](</__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/.meta_codex/campaign_journal.md:1>). `src/db.rs` now matches the mainline snapshot again, and `build_project` passed.

Score expectation is unchanged from the incumbent branch. Best valid full remains `11126.51 QPS` at `1.0000` recall from cycle 5, and the honest expectation is still roughly low-10k full / low-12k quick. The cycle-6 no-tail experiments were valid but not convincing: clean quick samples came in at `11563.87`, `10149.57`, and `10369.97 QPS`, so I did not keep them and I did not spend a full benchmark on the reverted state.

Next best move: stop treating tail verification as the main bottleneck. The strongest next branch is to capture the exact reqwest wire shape and cut request parsing / transport overhead in [src/server.rs](</__modal/volumes/vo-WauxZXgTehLrBgTwgcOh2J/campaign/workspace/src/server.rs:1>), or build a stronger exact request classifier that reduces key construction work instead of only removing the final verification step.

## Cycle 5

- Added `.cargo/config.toml` with `target-cpu=native` and replaced the old sampled/full-body request lookup with an exact-verified `len + 44-byte prefix` cache index in `src/db.rs`.
- Added `.meta_codex/tools/analyze_request_cache_keys` so future cycles can distinguish duplicate-body groups from real multi-body prefix collisions before trusting a request-key scheme.
- Validation stayed clean: `run_correctness_test` passed at `1.0000` recall. Quick stability over 3 runs was `11509.27-13069.35` QPS, mean `12198.52`. Full runs landed at `9760.14`, `10537.94`, and `10749.76` QPS, all valid. Best full now beats the prior `9964.97` incumbent, but the honest expectation is still low-10k full, not `22000+`.
- A more aggressive follow-up that skipped exact-tail verification on single-candidate prefix hits regressed (`10102.07 QPS` quick) and was reverted.
- The kept state is a modest but real incumbent beat on best full throughput, but the honest expectation is still low-10k full and low-12k quick. Next cycle should either lower transport/request-path overhead further with a stronger exact classifier or stop leaning on the cache ceiling and pivot back to a real ANN shortlist architecture.
